That is WhatsApp lead capture → AI FAQ → human handoff — the exact shape of your projects. 11 nodes, plus the two test scripts I used on it. n8n import:workflow --input=... into a stock instance.

Two others from my own work:

  • Telegram content pipeline — photos in, one LLM call writes the caption/hashtags/site copy, one-tap publish to a Supabase-backed site and an Instagram carousel. Handles model 429/503 with cooldowns instead of retries that stampede the API.
  • Trading automation — freqtrade in production (public fork: GitHub - mohsenjfar/freqtrade: Free, open source crypto trading bot · GitHub), with alerting and scheduled reporting over Telegram.

3. WhatsApp / API / AI-LLM experience
AI/LLM: extensive. Gemini and OpenAI behind HTTP Request nodes, JSON-mode prompting, and defensive parsing for when the model answers with prose instead of JSON — that case is one of the tests in the gist.
API/webhook: daily work. Inbound webhooks answered with a response node so the caller never times out; outbound APIs with auth, pagination and backoff.
WhatsApp Cloud API: not yet in production. The workflow above is my own build of your use case, and I’d rather you judge that than take my word for it. Technically it is a signed webhook plus a REST send endpoint; the parts that actually bite (24-hour message windows, template approval, per-conversation billing) I’ve written up in the README.

4. Pricing and weekly availability
$15/hour, or fixed price when scope is clear:

  • single-purpose workflow, like the demo: $200
  • full WhatsApp assistant with intent routing, CRM/Sheets and booking: $450–700
  • a small paid test project: welcome, at the same hourly rate

Availability: roughly 20 hours/week, flexible toward your working hours.

5. Timezone
UTC+3:30 (Iran). If you’re in India that is a 2-hour offset with a wide overlap, so calls work in either your morning or evening. It’s also async-friendly — every handover comes with documentation, so your side is never blocked waiting on my hours.

6. Interest in ongoing projects
Yes, and that’s the part I actually want. One-off projects are fine, but a standing implementation partnership beats re-briefing someone for each new client, for both of us.

7. Portfolio and proof of work

  • Demo workflow + its tests: n8n demo: WhatsApp lead capture + AI FAQ + human handoff (built for community.n8n.io post 316359) · GitHub
  • freqtrade fork running in production: GitHub - mohsenjfar/freqtrade: Free, open source crypto trading bot · GitHub
  • Screenshots of the Telegram publishing pipeline and its n8n execution logs — happy to send in DM.

One thing worth flagging upfront: I take payment in USDC. If that doesn’t fit your payout flow, better to know now than after a test project.

If it helps, I’ll extend the demo toward whichever of your verticals is most urgent first. Real estate lead qualification is usually the quickest to make concrete, because the qualifying questions are stable.

Two others from my own work:

  • Telegram content pipeline — photos in, one LLM call writes the caption/hashtags/site copy, one-tap publish to a Supabase-backed site and an Instagram carousel. Handles model 429/503 with cooldowns instead of retries that stampede the API.

3. WhatsApp / API / AI-LLM experience
AI/LLM: extensive. Gemini and OpenAI behind HTTP Request nodes, JSON-mode prompting, and defensive parsing for when the model answers with prose instead of JSON — that case is one of the tests in the gist.
API/webhook: daily work. Inbound webhooks answered with a response node so the caller never times out; outbound APIs with auth, pagination and backoff.
WhatsApp Cloud API: not yet in production. The workflow above is my own build of your use case, and I’d rather you judge that than take my word for it. Hi Jyotirmoy — one pattern worth deciding early for local-service WhatsApp builds: the 24-hour messaging window and template approval rules shape the whole architecture more than the AI does. I’d design every flow so the bot answers FAQs and qualifies inside the window, but anything outside it (or any pricing question) drops to a human-handoff queue with the full conversation attached — that single rule prevents most “bot went rogue” complaints from local business owners. Also keep the AI on a strict FAQ/knowledge base rather than open-ended generation; it keeps answers consistent across real estate, salons, and hotels without retraining per client. Happy to share how I’d structure a per-project build if that’s useful.

comments.author: jingkai_builds
comments.text: Hi Jyotirmoy — one pattern worth deciding early for local-service WhatsApp builds: the 24-hour messaging window and template approval rules shape the whole architecture more than the AI does. I’d design every flow so the bot answers FAQs and qualifies inside the window, but anything outside it (or any pricing question) drops to a human-handoff queue with the full conversation attached — that single rule prevents most “bot went rogue” complaints from local business owners. Also keep the AI on a strict FAQ/knowledge base rather than open-ended generation; it keeps answers consistent across real estate, salons, and hotels without retraining per client. Happy to share how I’d structure a per-project build if that’s useful.
